messages.subject: set hyper parameters for multiple
parts:
I have a model with several IID terms (random slopes, random intercepts model)
Can I set all of the hyper parameters for all IID terms with a single command, rather than specifying each time...

That is, rather than specifying in the formula  y~...f(var1, model='iid', prior='normal', param=c(a, b)) + f(var2, model='iid', prior='normal', param=c(a, b)) +  f(var3, model='iid', prior='normal', param=c(a, b))

can I just do: y~...f(var1, model='iid') + f(var2, model='iid') +  f(var3,model='iid')

and then set param=c(a,b) once in the call to inla()?

I want to test sensitivity to hyper params, so want to make it as easy as possible to change a & b..

Thanks

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] set hyper parameters for multiple
parts:
Hi Jim,

You can get most of the way there by using the newer method of prior specification.

hyper.iid = list(prec = list(prior = "normal", param=c(a,b)))
formula = y~...f(var1, model='iid', hyper = hyper.iid) + f(var2, model='iid', hyper = hyper.iid) +  f(var3, hyper = hyper.iid)

The example here shows how to do it: http://www.math.ntnu.no/%7Ehrue/r-inla.org/doc/prior/gaussian.pdf

Hope this helps,

Dan
